title: The Last Letter
text:
Short stories often depend on a single moment to reveal a great deal about a character. In the story below, a young woman named Eleanor finds an old letter in a dusty drawer. She reads it quietly at the kitchen table, and her hands begin to tremble. The letter, written decades earlier, reveals a secret that her grandmother had kept for fifty years.

Although Eleanor is shocked, she does not rush to confront her family. Instead, she spends the evening thinking about how little she really knew about the woman who raised her. By the morning, she has decided to visit the address written at the bottom of the letter. The story ends as she stands at the gate, unsure whether she is ready to knock.

questions.text: Where does Eleanor find the old letter?
What has Eleanor decided to do by the morning?
options: Visit the address on the letter

questions.text: How does Eleanor most likely feel about her grandmother after reading the letter?
options: She is certain she never really knew her grandmother
She is angry and wants to forget the letter
She feels bored by the discovery
She is sure her family has always been honest with her

questions.text: Why does the story end with Eleanor standing at the gate?
options: She has already decided to leave town
She is uncertain about taking the next step
She is waiting for her family to arrive

vocabulary.definition: to shake slightly, usually because of fear or strong emotion
to face someone in order to deal with a problem or disagreement
covered with fine dust, usually because it has not been cleaned for a long time

paragraph_translations: Krótkie opowiadania często opierają się na jednym momencie, który ujawnia bardzo wiele o bohaterze. W poniższej historii młoda kobieta o imieniu Eleanor znajduje stary list w zakurzonej szufladzie. Czyta go po cichu przy kuchennym stole, a jej dłonie zaczynają drżeć. List, napisany dziesiątki lat wcześniej, ujawnia sekret, który jej babcia przechowywała przez pięćdziesiąt lat.

Choć Eleanor jest zszokowana, nie spieszy się, by stawić czoło rodzinie. Zamiast tego spędza wieczór, myśląc o tym, jak mało naprawdę wiedziała o kobiecie, która ją wychowała. Rano postanawia odwiedzić adres zapisany na dole listu. Historia kończy się, gdy stoi przy bramie, niepewna, czy jest gotowa zapukać.
